original_question: Suppose an integer sequence a(n) has the property that for every connected ℓ-step nilmanifold X and every irrational nilrotation b on X, the sequence (b^{a(n)} Γ) is equidistributed in X, and for every r ∈ N the set {n ∈ N : r divides a(n)} has positive upper density. Must a(n) then be good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations?
target_in_paper: Section 4.3, Problem 4 (“Sufficient conditions for ℓ-recurrence”), which asks for a nilmanifold/equidistribution criterion implying that a single integer sequence is good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact two hypotheses and the exact conclusion of the paper’s target problem: equidistribution of (b^{a(n)}Γ) on every connected ℓ-step nilmanifold under every irrational nilrotation, plus positive upper density of the divisibility sets {n : r divides a(n)} for every r, with the desired conclusion that a(n) be good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
missing_details: It should explicitly fix ℓ ∈ N; in the paper, ℓ is a fixed parameter appearing both in “connected ℓ-step nilmanifold” and in “good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

It should write the nilmanifold as X = G/Γ and specify that b ∈ G acts on X by left translation, since the paper’s nilsystems/nilrotations are formulated that way. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
It should define “irrational nilrotation” exactly as the paper does: b is irrational if the orbit (b^nΓ)_{n∈N} is equidistributed on X. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
It should make “positive upper density” explicit if the question is to be fully stand-alone; the paper flags this notion in the introduction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))

It should unpack the conclusion using the paper’s definition: for every probability space (Y, 𝒴, μ), every commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T1, ..., Tℓ, and every A ∈ 𝒴 with μ(A) > 0, there exists n ∈ N with a(n) ≠ 0 such that μ(A ∩ T1^{-a(n)}A ∩ ··· ∩ Tℓ^{-a(n)}A) > 0. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It should make clear that the same single sequence a(n) is used in every commuting iterate; the paper’s conclusion is not about an arbitrary ℓ-tuple of possibly different sequences. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To match the paper’s status and wording, it should be framed as an open problem (“Show that ...” / “Is it true that ... ?”), not as an established theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
refined_question: Fix ℓ ∈ N. Let a: N → Z be an integer sequence such that: (i) for every connected ℓ-step nilmanifold X = G/Γ and every irrational nilrotation b ∈ G on X (that is, the orbit (b^nΓ)_{n∈N} is equidistributed in X), the sequence (b^{a(n)}Γ)_{n∈N} is equidistributed in X; and (ii) for every r ∈ N, the set {n ∈ N : r divides a(n)} has positive upper density. Is it then true that a(n) is good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations, i.e. for every probability space (Y, 𝒴, μ), every commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T1, ..., Tℓ: Y → Y, and every A ∈ 𝒴 with μ(A) > 0, there exists n ∈ N with a(n) ≠ 0 such that μ(A ∩ T1^{-a(n)}A ∩ ··· ∩ Tℓ^{-a(n)}A) > 0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
justification: The draft is already a close paraphrase of the paper’s intended question, and the nearest official formulation is Problem 4 in §4.3. The nearby context is essential: the problem is posed immediately after the Kamae–Mendès-France theorem giving the ℓ = 1 model criterion, and after the paper explains that an analogous proof for ℓ ≥ 2 is unavailable because no suitable generalization of the single-correlation identity is known. To make your draft fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must import the paper’s definitions of nilmanifold/nilrotation and, especially, the exact meaning of “good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations.” I left equivalent_formulation as null because, although §3.1 gives general correspondence-principle reformulations of recurrence notions, the paper does not isolate Problem 4 itself as a separate named equivalent formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
